extra.message: Authentication SQL injection. The query on line 7 is built by concatenating the user-controlled request body fields `username` and `password` directly into the SQL string, which is executed on line 9 via db.one(q). A payload such as username=`' OR '1'='1' --` bypasses authentication entirely.

SQL injection in getProduct(). The `product_id` value comes from the attacker-controlled query parameter `id` (routes/products.js:47) and is concatenated into the SQL string on line 14 before being executed on line 16.

SQL injection in search(). The attacker-controlled query parameter `q` (routes/products.js:67) is concatenated into the ILIKE clauses on line 21 and executed on line 23. A payload such as `' UNION SELECT name,password,... FROM users --` can exfiltrate arbitrary data.

SQL injection in purchase(). All cart fields (mail, product_name, username, product_id, address, ship_date, phone, price) originate from the request (routes/products.js:104-116) and are concatenated into the INSERT statement on lines 29-38 before execution on line 40.

SQL injection in get_purchased(). The `username` value (req.session.user_name, which is set to the submitted login username at routes/login.js:30) is concatenated into the query on line 46 and executed on line 48. Combined with the login SQL injection, an attacker can set their session username to a SQL payload and read all users' purchases.

No CSRF protection is configured anywhere (no csurf/anti-CSRF token, no SameSite cookie, and the session cookie has secure:false). The state-changing /products/buy endpoint is reachable via GET and POST without a token (routes/products.js:89-145), so an attacker page can silently create purchases in a victim's session.
The Express framework is initialized without disabling its default `X-Powered-By: Express` response header, disclosing the server framework and aiding attacker fingerprinting.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: The express-session signing secret is hardcoded in source (`ñasddfilhpaf78h78032h780g780fg780asg780dsbovncubuyvqy`). Anyone who can read the source can forge a valid connect.sid cookie and impersonate any user, resulting in authentication bypass.

cwe: CWE-547: Use of Hard-coded, Security-relevant Constants

extra.message: The session cookie is configured with `secure: false`, so it is sent over plain HTTP and can be intercepted on the network. No SameSite attribute is set, which also weakens CSRF defenses.

cwe: CWE-614: Sensitive Cookie in HTTPS Session Without 'Secure' Attribute

extra.message: Open redirect. `returnurl` is taken from the request (query parameter on GET /login at line 12, request body on POST /login/auth at line 23) and passed to res.redirect() without validation, allowing redirection to an arbitrary external site (e.g. /login?returnurl=https://evil.com).

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site ('Open Redirect')

extra.message: Reflected XSS. The search term `q` is passed as `in_query` and rendered with the unescaped EJS tag `<%- in_query %>`. Requesting /products/search?q=<script>...</script> executes attacker JavaScript in the victim's browser.

extra.message: Reflected XSS. The `returnurl` query parameter is rendered unescaped with `<%-returnurl%>` inside a hidden input value. A payload such as /login?returnurl="><script>alert(1)</script> breaks out of the attribute and executes script.

Purchase fields (product_id, product_name, mail, phone, ship_date, address) are accepted from the /products/buy request, stored in the purchases table, and rendered here with unescaped `<%- %>` tags. An attacker can submit a malicious address/phone that executes script when the purchased-products page is viewed.

extra.message: Regular expression Denial of Service (ReDoS). The email regex on line 120 contains nested quantifiers `(([\-.]|[_]+)?([a-zA-Z0-9]+))*` and is tested against the attacker-controlled `cart.mail` value on line 121. A crafted input such as many alphanumerics followed by `!` causes catastrophic backtracking and hangs the Node.js event loop (see attacks/evil_regex/attack_1.sh).

Log injection / log forging. The attacker-controlled `username` request body value is concatenated directly into a log4js log message without sanitization, allowing an attacker to inject newlines and forge log entries (see attacks/log_injection.sh).

cwe: CWE-117: Improper Output Neutralization for Logs

extra.message: Hardcoded database credentials. The PostgreSQL connection strings embed the username and password `postgres:postgres` in source code (also lines 12 and 20). Secrets in source are exposed to anyone with repository access and cannot be rotated without a code change.
